tool.name: SEM fiber analysis
tool.description: segment fibers and measure their diameters with FIJI and DiameterJ
tool.command: mkdir -p results && export ANALYSIS_RESULTS_DIR='results' && ln -s '$input_image' input.tif && set -- --input input.tif --output results --segmentation '$segmentation.workflow' && #if $segmentation.workflow in ('recursive-srm', 'srm-auto-thresholding', 'all'): set -- "\$@" --srm-q '$segmentation.srm_q' && #end if #if $calibration.source == 'pixel_size': set -- "\$@" --pixel-size-um '$calibration.pixel_size_um' && #else: set -- "\$@" --hfw-um '$calibration.hfw_um' && #end if #if $analysis_mode == 'qc': set -- "\$@" --skip-diameterj && #end if set -- "\$@" --crop-bottom '$advanced.crop_bottom' && #if $analysis_mode == 'diameterj': /usr/local/bin/sem-analysis "\$@" && python3 '$__tool_directory__/convert_radius_plots.py' results #else: /usr/local/bin/sem-analysis "\$@" #end if

param.name: input_image
param.label: SEM micrograph
param.help: A 2-D TIFF image. RGB TIFFs are converted to grayscale.

validator.message: Horizontal field width must be greater than zero
Pixel size must be greater than zero

param.name: crop_bottom
param.label: Crop from bottom (pixels)
param.help: Removes the SEM instrument footer before analysis.

tool.help:
**What it does**
This tool prepares an SEM micrograph for DiameterJ, creates a binary fiber mask, and computes an independent Python diameter quality-control estimate. In full mode it also runs the validated DiameterJ 1.018 workflow under a virtual display.
The tool provides Fiji Auto Thresholding, SRM with Auto Thresholding, and Recursive SRM workflows. Every generated mask receives an independent skeleton/distance-transform QC.
**Input image**
The input must be a TIFF image. A two-dimensional grayscale image is used directly. An RGB TIFF is converted to grayscale by averaging its first three channels. Other dimensional layouts, such as image stacks or time series, are not supported.
**Segmentation workflow**
* **Auto Thresholding** applies all 17 concrete Fiji Auto Threshold v1.18.0 methods directly to the cropped image: Default, Huang, Huang2, Intermodes, IsoData, Li, MaxEntropy, Mean, MinError(I), Minimum, Moments, Otsu, Percentile, RenyiEntropy, Shanbhag, Triangle, and Yen. * **SRM with Auto Thresholding** applies one Statistical Region Merging pass at the selected ``q``, converts the result to 8-bit, and applies all 17 Auto Threshold methods. * **Recursive SRM** runs exactly one recursive workflow. It successively applies SRM at ``q``, ``q/2``, ``q/4``, and ``q/8`` (with a minimum of 1), then applies all 17 threshold methods to the final SRM image. It therefore reports exactly 17 segmentations * **All Fiji segmentation workflows** runs all three workflows and produces 51 candidate masks.
**Analysis mode**
* **Full DiameterJ analysis** creates the selected segmentation masks and QC results, then runs DiameterJ 1.018 on every mask. Candidates are not rejected based on their black-pixel fraction, so review the segmentation and overlay montages when a threshold method produces an implausible mask. * **Segmentation and Python QC only** skips DiameterJ analysis. It is faster and is useful for comparing candidate masks before a full run.
**Calibration and interpretation**
Python QC measurements are reported in pixels and micrometres. Choose one of the following calibration sources:
* **Horizontal field width** is the physical width represented by the entire uncropped image. Pixel size is calculated as ``HFW / image width in pixels``. The default is 27.04 µm and should be replaced with the value recorded by the microscope for the input image. * **Pixel size** directly specifies micrometres per pixel. Use this when the calibrated pixel spacing is already known.
Cropping the bottom does not change image width, so it does not alter an HFW-derived pixel size. DiameterJ runs in its validated native-pixel mode because physical calibration can change its legacy particle-size filtering. Use the ``pixel_size_um`` field in ``python_qc_summary.csv`` when converting DiameterJ measurements to physical units.
**Segmentation options**
* **Crop from bottom** removes a fixed number of pixel rows before analysis. The default of 59 is intended for an SEM annotation or instrument footer. Set it to 0 when the image contains no footer. It must be smaller than image height. * **SRM granularity (q)** controls region merging in SRM with Auto Thresholding, Recursive SRM, and All modes. It must be positive. Larger values generally preserve more, smaller regions; lower values generally merge regions more aggressively. The default is 100.
**Outputs**
All generated files are returned as one list collection in the Galaxy history. Each workflow produces two PNG review sheets: a segmentation montage containing the cropped original and every binary mask, and an overlay montage containing the original and every boundary overlay. It also produces each candidate as a separate, display-ready PNG and as a matching TIFF used for DiameterJ analysis. Each individual workflow produces 17 segmented PNG images; All produces 51.
Dataset names retain the input stem, segmentation family, SRM settings where applicable, and threshold method. For each mask, QC-only mode also includes a boundary-overlay PNG and diameter-samples CSV; the collection contains one Python QC summary CSV. Full mode adds the DiameterJ total summary, comparison image, pore data, radius histogram, characteristic lengths, and radius plot for each mask. Every DiameterJ radius-plot TIFF is converted to PNG before Galaxy discovers the collection.
The resulting collection size depends on the workflow and analysis mode. Full-analysis counts are maximums: if legacy DiameterJ stops producing files for a problematic threshold candidate, completed results are retained and the stalled Fiji process is terminated rather than leaving the Galaxy job running:
* Auto Thresholding: 71 QC-only or 173 full results. * SRM with Auto Thresholding: 71 QC-only or 173 full results. * Recursive SRM: 71 QC-only or 173 full results. * All Fiji segmentation workflows: 207 QC-only or 513 full results.
The QC diameter samples are distance-transform measurements on skeleton pixels. They are intended as an independent quality check; DiameterJ output is the primary result in full-analysis mode.
